chains.summary: Calm, inquiry, contentment and good company are the four gatekeepers at the door of freedom. Befriend one with full effort and the others follow.
chains.title: The four gatekeepers

verses.m: From constant contact with good people, discernment is born; and the fruits of the tree of discernment are both enjoyment and freedom.
verses.sa: नित्यं सज्जनसंपर्काद्विवेक उपजायते । विवेकपादपस्यैव भोगमोक्षौ फले स्मृतौ ॥

verses.m: One whose whole being is armoured in the nectar of calm is not pierced by sorrows, as arrows cannot pierce a diamond rock.
verses.sa: सुसंनद्धसमस्ताङ्गं प्रशमामृतवर्मणा । वेधयन्ति न दुःखानि शरा वज्रशिलामिव ॥

verses.m: Sharpened by inquiry, the mind sees the highest. Inquiry is the great medicine for the long illness of worldly life.
verses.sa: विचारात्तीक्ष्णतामेत्य धीः पश्यति परं पदम् । दीर्घसंसाररोगस्य विचारो हि महौषधम् ॥

chains.summary: A person is poor when his craving is large. When the mind is content, there is no distinction between rich and poor.
chains.title: Who is rich, who is poor

verses.m: We are content here with bark garments, you with silk; the contentment is equal, and the difference makes no difference. He is poor whose craving is vast. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?
verses.sa: वयमिह परितुष्टा वल्कलैस्त्वं दुकूलैः सम इव परितोषो निर्विशेषो विशेषः । स तु भवतु दरिद्रो यस्य तृष्णा विशाला मनसि च परितुष्टे कोऽर्थवान्को दरिद्रः ॥

verses.m: Those always delighted by contentment have joy that is undivided; the others, minds crowded with greed for money, never kill their craving. So for whom did fate make wealth, and what kind of place is it? Mount Meru, whose golden glory ends in itself, does not appeal to me.
verses.sa: ये सन्तोषनिरन्तरप्रमुदितास्तेषां न भिन्ना मुदो ये त्वन्ये धनलुब्धसंकुलधियस्तेषां न तृष्णा हता । इत्थं कस्य कृते कृतः स विधिना कीदृक्पदं सम्पदां स्वात्मन्येव समाप्तहेममहिमा मेरुर्न मे रोचते ॥

chains.summary: A person with a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with what comes has no enmity, no quarrel, no hanging hope, and no dread. For such a person, every direction is full of joy.
chains.title: No grudge, no hope, no fear

verses.m: "Tell me, what effort does this path take? No yoga, no sacrifices, no chanting, austerities or fasts. Only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with whatever comes."
verses.sa: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥

verses.m: "Holding no grudge and picking no quarrel, with neither craving nor fear, every direction is joyful to him. He starts nothing out of craving for results, clings to no house, wants no honour, is free of wrongdoing and anger, skilled and wise."
verses.sa: बैर न बिग्रह आस न त्रासा। सुखमय ताहि सदा सब आसा॥ अनारंभ अनिकेत अमानी। अनघ अरोष दच्छ बिग्यानी ॥

chains.summary: Without knowing there is no trust. Without trust there is no love. Without love devotion does not hold. No one finds rest without contentment. A boat does not move without water.
chains.title: Knowing, trust, love

verses.m: Without knowing his greatness, no trust forms; without trust, no love; and without love, devotion is not firm, just as, king of birds, oil does not stay on water.
verses.sa: जानें बिनु न होइ परतीती। बिनु परतीति होइ नहिं प्रीती॥ प्रीति बिना नहिं भगति दिढ़ाई। जिमि खगपति जल कै चिकनाई ॥

verses.m: Can anyone find rest without natural contentment, friend? Can a boat move without water, though you strain and wear yourself out with a million efforts?
verses.sa: कोउ बिश्राम कि पाव तात सहज संतोष बिनु। चलै कि जल बिनु नाव कोटि जतन पचि पचि मरिअ ॥

depicts.m: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
depicts.sa: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
depicts.why: Is at peace with a whole life, blunders included.

gloss: Being at ease with what has come. One of Vasishtha's four gatekeepers; the Yaksha is told it is the highest happiness.

hero.m: ever content, steady in practice, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding given to me, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
hero.sa: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥

loci.m: ever content, steady in practice, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding given to me, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
loci.sa: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥

loci.m: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
loci.sa: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥

loci.m: Yaksha: 'What is the best of good fortunes? The best of riches? The best of gains? The best of joys?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the best fortune; learning is the best wealth; health is the best gain; contentment is the highest happiness.'
loci.sa: धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् / लाभानामुत्तमं किंस्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमं धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यंधनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् / लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
practices.why: Shows enjoying what is present is named as the practice.

practices.m: No one in this world gains real wealth through greed. Enough of greed, my son. Be at peace.
practices.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
practices.sa: न लोभादर्थसंपत्तिर्नराणामिह दृश्यते / तदलं तात लोभेन प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ ॥

practices.m: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
practices.sa: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
practices.why: Shows contentment named as a form of devotion.

practices.m: Will I ever live like this? By the grace of kind Raghunath, will I take on the nature of a saint: always content with what comes, wanting nothing from anyone, always devoted to others' good, keeping my vow in mind, deed and word; hearing very harsh words and not burning in that fire; free of pride, even and cool of mind, speaking of others' virtues and not their faults; letting go of the body's worries, bearing joy and sorrow with an even mind?
practices.sa: कबहुँक हौं यहि रहनि रहौंगो। श्रीरघुनाथ-कृपालु-कृपातें संत-सुभाव गहौंगो॥ ९॥ जथालाभसंतोष सदा, काहू सों कछु न चहांगो। पर-हित-निरत निरंतर, मन क्रम बचन नेम निबहौंगो॥ … परुष बचन अति दुसह श्रवन सुनि तेहि पावक न दहांगो। बिगत मान, सम सीतल मन, पर-गुन नहिं दोष कहाँगो॥ ३॥ परिहरि देह-जनित चिंता, दुख-सुख समबुद्धि सहोंगो।

practices.m: Four gatekeepers are named at the door of freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and the company of good people. Take refuge in even one of them with full effort, setting all else aside; when one is won, all four come under your control.
practices.sa: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः ॥ एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः ॥
practices.why: Contentment is named as a door, not a reward.

practices.m: Bear the good fortune of others, even though it is not with you. Wise people know how to enjoy good fortune even when it belongs to someone else; good fortune drains away from the one who resents.
practices.sa: सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा / अन्यत्रापि सतीं लक्ष्मीं कुशला भुञ्जते नराः / अभिनिष्यन्दते देही श्रीभूतश्च द्विषज्जनात्

practices.m: "Tell me, what effort does this path take? No yoga, no sacrifices, no chanting, austerities or fasts. Only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with whatever comes."
practices.sa: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥

stories.l: When the mind is content, nobody is richer than you.
stories.s: An ascetic tells a king who ignores him that learning equals wealth, that contentment in bark equals contentment in silk, and that pride over a few towns is a fever.
stories.t: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king

stories.l: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
stories.s: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.

stories.l: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
stories.s: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
stories.t: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps

stories.l: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
stories.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
stories.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
